data.title: China stocks edge up as industrial profit growth buoys sentiment; tech leads gains
data.description:
By Summer Zhen

China and Hong Kong stocks rose on Friday as robust industrial profit growth buoyed market sentiment, with AI and chipmaking shares leading the advance.

** China's blue-chip CSI300 Index climbed 0.2% by the lunch break, while the Shanghai Composite Index gained 0.3%.

** Hong Kong's benchmark Hang Seng (.HIS) index was up 0.9%.

** Profit growth at China's industrial firms accelerated in October to the fastest in five months, mainly driven by AI-related industries and upstream sectors, although broader economic momentum remained subdued.

** Industrial figures gave market confidence a modest lift as stocks rebounded from a steep recent selloff, while investors assessed renewed tariff risks.

** In mainland A-shares, semiconductor materials and equipment stocks (.CSI931743) rallied as much as 8%, while cloud computing (.CSI931469) jumped 6% as investors bought the dip and bet on domestic tech substitution.

** In Hong Kong, Hang Seng Tech gained more than 3% by midday, with AI startup Minimax and Shanghai Iluvatar CoreX Semiconductor bouncing over 10% each.

** In contrast, the aviation and energy sectors were among the biggest underperformers.

** US President Donald Trump proposed new maximum tariff rates of 20% to 40% on Wednesday on goods from 14 major trading partners including China, Japan ​and the European Union.

** However, BofA Securities analysts believe the move is unlikely to reignite trade tensions.

** "The headline overstates the incremental tariff increase, and the proposal remains broadly consistent with the existing US-China trade framework," the bank said.

** The smaller Shenzhen index was up 2.32%, the start-up board ChiNext Composite index was higher by 3.79% and Shanghai's tech-focused STAR50 index was up 4.43%​.

data.title: ReFuels Q2 2027: CNG Fuels nearly doubles H1 adjusted EBITDA, expects full-year earnings at upper end of guidance
data.description:
27 November 2026: ReFuels N.V. (ticker: REFL) ("ReFuels"), one of Europe's leading suppliers of renewable biomethane (Bio-CNG) for the decarbonisation of heavy goods vehicles, today releases its interim report for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 for July–September 2026.

Highlights:

  • H1 2027 adj. EBITDA increased 98% to GBP 8.9 million, compared to H1 2026, with a third consecutive quarter of positive station network contribution
  • CNG Fuels FY 2027 adj. EBITDA guidance of GBP 16–20 million expected at the upper end of the range
  • Nearly 200 6x2 Bio-CNG trucks operating across 25 fleets, supporting broader adoption among UK heavy-duty operators
  • EU to review heavy-duty vehicle CO₂ standards, potentially paving the way for greater recognition of renewable fuels
  • Opened 17th high-capacity station, with two more under construction and MRS fleet expected to grow from 11 to 14 units
  • Continued network expansion supports CNG Fuels’ target of more than 8,000 Bio-CNG HGVs on UK roads by 2030

Philip Fjeld, CEO and co-founder of ReFuels, said:

“The case for Bio-CNG remains compelling, with significantly lower emissions, greater security of supply and a proven long-term fuel cost advantage over diesel. Adoption continues to broaden, with nearly 200 of the larger 6x2 trucks now on the road and more coming soon. Together with our station build-out, this will enable future growth. CNG Fuels delivered its third consecutive quarter of positive station network contribution, reflecting improving economies of scale, alongside strong certificate earnings. We now expect FY2027 adjusted EBITDA to be at the upper end of our guidance range of GBP 16–20 million.”

The second quarter 2027 interim report and presentation are attached and available at: https://refuels.com/investor-relations/

ReFuels will present the second quarter 2027 results today at 10:00 CET. The webcast will be hosted by CEO Philip Fjeld and CFO Baden Gowrie-Smith. Please register for the presentation via the following link: https://bit.ly/4AMuOsP

For further information, please contact:

Philip Fjeld, CEO, ReFuels N.V.

Tel: +44 7976 159 833

Email: Philip.Fjeld@refuels.com

Baden Gowrie-Smith, MD & CFO, ReFuels N.V.

Tel: +44 7768 007 009

Email: baden@refuels.com

About ReFuels

ReFuels is decarbonising Europe's truck fleet through its 40% ownership of CNG Fuels – a fully integrated clean fuel infrastructure platform combining sourcing of renewable biomethane (Bio-CNG), Renewable Transport Fuel Certificates (RTFCs), and ownership and operation of the UK's largest clean fuel station network. By the end of 2028, the target is to reach capacity to serve 20,000 heavy goods vehicles per day, with the long-term ambition to become Europe's leading integrated supplier of alternative fuels for commercial fleets. For further information, please visit www.refuels.com.

This information has been submitted pursuant to the Securities Trading Act § 5-12 and MAR. The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact persons set out above, at 2026-11-27 06:00 CET.

data.title: Energy Holdings Q3 2026: Strong performance, backlog growth and strategic progress
data.description:
Limassol, Cyprus - November 27, 2026: SED Energy Holdings Plc ("Energy Holdings") delivered continued positive financial and operational development in the third quarter of 2026, driven by a fully utilized Energy Drilling fleet, partly offset by lower activity in SeaBird Exploration. During the quarter, Energy Holdings and Ventura Offshore Holding Ltd. signed a letter of intent to combine, creating a more diversified platform with greater scale and a stronger capital markets profile. Closing of the proposed combination is expected during the first quarter of 2027.

“Energy Holdings delivered a solid third quarter, with important progress on both contracts and strategic initiatives. New contract awards across both businesses strengthen contract coverage into 2027, and the proposed combination with Ventura Offshore remains on track for closing in the first quarter,” said Kurt M. Waldeland, CEO.

Distributions for the second half of 2026 have been deferred until after completion of the proposed combination. This is a timing consequence of the transaction agreements, which do not permit distributions to shareholders before closing. Energy Holdings remains fully committed to distributing available excess liquidity to shareholders and will resume distributions once the transaction completes. On a standalone basis, Energy Holdings maintains its full-year distribution guidance of USD 90-110 million and will provide an update on the deferred amount at closing.

“Looking ahead, we are seeing encouraging signs that activity in our markets is improving. Underlying demand for tender-assist drilling in Southeast Asia remains strong, while tendering activity and visibility in marine seismic are improving. We expect to continue adding to our backlog in the coming months, and remain focused on converting this activity into high utilization, strong cash generation and sustainable shareholder returns,” Waldeland continued.

Q3 2026 highlights:

  • Revenue of USD 66.4 million and EBITDA of USD 37.0 million, with last twelve months EBITDA of USD 149 million, supported by continued high activity in Energy Drilling.
  • Net cash flow from operating activities amounted to USD 107.0 million in the first nine months of 2026.
  • Net interest-bearing debt1 was USD 22.7 million at quarter-end, corresponding to 0.2x LTM adjusted EBITDA.
  • Energy Drilling delivered strong performance with economic utilization of 99%. SeaBird completed the five-year classing of Fulmar Explorer and mobilized Eagle Explorer, resulting in lower utilization in the period.
  • After quarter-end, Energy Drilling secured contracts for the T-16 and SeaBird secured a new contract for Fulmar Explorer starting in late 2026.
  • Firm revenue backlog was USD 367 million, including contracts awarded after quarter-end.
  • Due to transaction-related restrictions associated with the contemplated combination with Ventura Offshore, shareholder distributions for the second half of 2026 will be announced after completion of the transaction.
  • Standalone full-year distribution guidance of USD 90–110 million reiterated, of which USD 50 million has been declared for the first half of 2026.

Third quarter 2026 presentation

The third quarter 2026 materials are enclosed and available on the company's website: www.energyholdings.cy/investors/financial-reports/.

Energy Holdings will present its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 in a live audio webcast today at 10:00 CET, hosted by Kurt M. Waldeland, Chief Executive Officer, Sveinung Alvestad, Chief Financial Officer, and Viggo Pedersen, Chief Investment Officer.

The presentation will be followed by a Q&A session and questions may be submitted in writing at any time during the event. A recording of the webcast will be made available on the company's website after the live event has been concluded.

Webcast link: https://events.streamhub.no/viewer-registration/pQZLXD63/register

For more information, please contact:

Investor Relations: ir@energyholdings.cy

Press: contact@energyholdings.cy

About SED Energy Holdings Plc

SED Energy Holdings Plc (ticker code "ENH") is a strong industrial partner with a diversified portfolio of resilient, cash-generative assets supported by a robust revenue backlog and a conservative capital structure. Energy Holdings' primary focus is on distributing all excess liquidity to shareholders, while also pursuing disciplined, value-accretive growth. For more information, please visit www.energyholdings.cy.

data.title: Coal India unit Mahanadi makes muted debut, valued at $9.6 billion
data.description:
Shares of Coal India unit Mahanadi Coalfields (MHAN.NS) made a subdued debut on Indian stock exchanges on Friday, following a $963 million initial public offering earlier this week.

The stock opened at 134 rupees on the National Stock Exchange, listing at a discount to its issue price of 136 rupees.

Shares of the company were last trading up 2.24% at 137 rupees, giving the company a market valuation of $9.59 billion.

Mahanadi Coalfields accounts for about a fifth of India's coal production and is the largest coal-producing unit of state-run Coal India.

Coal India, the world's biggest coal miner, is central to India's efforts to boost domestic production and reduce reliance on imports, as renewable energy capacity has yet to meet the country's growing power needs.

The listing comes during a year of strong activity in India's primary market, with marquee offerings from billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms and National Stock Exchange of India attracting major global investors.

Mahanadi Coalfields' IPO, which was entirely an offer-for-sale from Coal India, received bids for 1.5 times the shares on offer, with the portions set aside for retail and non-institutional investors not getting fully booked.

Mahanadi Coalfields is the third unit of state-owned Coal India to go public in 2026, after Bharat Coking Coal and Central Mine Planning & Design Institute .

($1 = 92.4450 Indian rupees)

data.title: Tata Steel's APL Apollo deal is 'ugly' due to structural flaws: IiAS MD Amit Tandon
data.description:
Tata Steel’s proposed transaction with APL Apollo has inherent structural infirmities and is 'ugly' in its current form, according to Amit Tandon, Managing Director at IiAS.

While the acquisition creates a 7.5 million-tonne entity and strengthens Tata Steel's downstream businesses, Tandon warned that the current framework leaves shareholders with very little say in the process.

The only opportunity for minority shareholders to intervene will arise when APL Apollo seeks approval for its borrowing of ₹28,000 crore. Tandon suggested this vote could serve as a possible deterrent to the deal.

"If they were to say that look, you can't borrow anymore at this stage, that could be one possible deterrence to the deal," he said, adding that his firm's initial read gives investors an opportunity to vote against the transaction.

Instead of the current arrangement, Tandon argued Tata Steel should have executed a straight purchase from APL Apollo's promoters, followed by an open offer to shareholders. He noted that taking on ₹28,000 crore in debt will be difficult to reduce through existing cash flows. This would require bringing in fresh equity, which would dilute shareholders at current prices.

Addressing whether Tata Steel could salvage the deal by sweetening the offer, Tandon expressed doubt due to the structure's fundamental flaws and the sharp drop in APL Apollo's share price to ₹1,400. "If it were at ₹2,300-2,400 and the Tatas had made an open offer, you would expect a different acceptance ratio," he explained. At ₹1,400, he noted that nearly everyone would tender their shares, which would significantly reduce the probability of an investor being able to exit their stock.

The transaction may also face regulatory scrutiny. Tandon pointed out that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has introduced a 'purpose and effect' regulation to examine whether economic interests are being transferred in ways that are not immediately obvious in the first instance.

"Maybe SEBI was going to kind of examine it, and therefore you will have some of these breaks which come in," he said, indicating the transaction may ultimately require a complete rework.

data.title: Parties to negotiate after no one wins majority in New Zealand election
data.description:
New Zealand's ruling coalition fell short of winning a parliamentary majority, final results of the November 7 election showed on Friday, leaving Prime Minister Christopher Luxon needing the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to form government.

Luxon said his centre-right National Party would work with its coalition partners, ACT and New Zealand First, and Opportunity to form government and avoid the need for a fresh election.

Opportunity's leader Qiulae Wong said she would negotiate with National as the party with the largest number of seats. That was consistent with statements she made before the election result was known. However, she has also said previously that Opportunity was prepared to speak with other parties.

WHERE DO THINGS STAND?

The final vote count showed the incumbent coalition of National, the right-wing ACT Party and the nationalist New Zealand First won 65 seats in the 130-seat parliament, one short of a majority, according to the Electoral Commission results.

Opportunity, contesting its first election, won seven seats.

On the left, Labour, the Green Party and Te Pati Maori hold 58 seats. This would not be enough seats to form a government even with the support of Opportunity.

The possibility remains that parties from either bloc could join forces to create a majority, such as in 2017 when Labour and NZ First reached a deal that made Jacinda Ardern prime minister.

WHAT IS THE PROCESS?

While there have been some informal meetings between parties since the election, now that the parties know how many seats they need to form a ​government, more formal negotiations can begin.

Along with policies, key ministerial appointments such as deputy prime minister, foreign minister and finance minister can all be part of negotiations.

Parties can sign either coalition agreements or looser alliances known as confidence-and-supply agreements. Under ​those deals, a smaller party agrees to support a government on key votes, without taking cabinet seats or being part of the government.

WHEN MIGHT NEW ZEALAND GET ​A GOVERNMENT?

Coalition negotiations lasted 40 days after the 2023 election, with National, ACT and New Zealand First signing their agreements on November 24. If negotiations follow a similar time frame, a government could be formed before Christmas.

However, since New Zealand introduced a proportional electoral system in 1996, only coalitions of up to three parties have ever been needed to form a majority. With four parties needing to reach agreement, it could take longer.

Parliament has to meet six weeks after the writs are returned. If no recounts are ordered, writs will be returned on December 3 and parliament must meet on or before January 14.

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER SIX WEEKS?

If a government hasn't been formed, parliament will still meet and lawmakers will be sworn in and a speaker elected.

The following day, parliament would be officially opened, the governor-general would deliver a speech and then a lawmaker could move to adjourn the house. This would mean that negotiations to form government could continue.

Governor-General Cindy Kiro said in a speech earlier this year that if it became clear that no government could be formed, another election may be required.

"The caretaker Prime Minister would be expected to consult other parties and seek majority support for calling a new election," she said.

WHO IS IN CHARGE UNTIL ​THEN?

The incumbent ⁠government, the National-led coalition, will continue to operate as a caretaker government while the new government is formed.

According to New Zealand's parliamentary website, a caretaker government can continue the normal business of the country but cannot make any significant ​decisions on its own except in an emergency or crisis.
